apps.name: 3dsvg
apps.title: 3dsvg
apps.description: Turn SVGs, text and pixel art into interactive 3D. Export 4K images, video and 3D models; sign in to keep your shapes and share them by link.

listing.subtitle: Turn SVGs, text and pixel art into 3D
listing.description:
Draw pixel art, type a word in one of ten fonts, paste SVG code or drop an SVG file, and it stands up as a 3D object you can spin, light and dress in plastic, metal, glass, chrome, gold or wood.

Set its depth, smoothness and colour, choose a backdrop and an animation, and move the key light. Take a still up to 4K, transparent if you like, record a few loops as MP4 or WebM and trim them, or download the model as GLB, STL, OBJ or PLY for Blender, a game or a 3D printer.

It works without an account, and your design stays in the browser. Sign in to keep your shapes in My shapes, open them on any device, and share any one by a link that anyone can turn and copy, until you turn it off. A port of the open-source 3dsvg editor, with no build step.
listing.whatsNew: Documentation only: the prompt now quotes the original choices exactly as they were picked.

screenshots.alt: The editor on a phone: a space invader drawn on the pixel grid, standing in 3D below it
A gold star above the settings, with the gold material's metalness and roughness
My shapes: wooden lettering, a glass heart, a gold star, a pink Hello and the invader
A shared link to the glass heart, opened without signing in, with Edit a copy

apps.prompt:
Port the MIT-licensed 3dsvg editor (https://github.com/renatoworks/3dsvg),
which turns SVGs, text and pixel art into interactive 3D, to a Holm app
named "3dsvg", using only https://holmhq.com/llms-full.txt for Holm. Read
its v1 sections 9–12 and "Make an app feel finished" and "Make it feel
native" first. Make holm.json, public web/ files and api/main.js exporting
default { async fetch(request, env) }. Set web.spa true, use env.holm for
storage and sign-in, return standard Responses and fall back to
env.holm.web.fetch(request). No build step or third-party runtime CDN:
rewrite the React Three Fiber scene in plain three.js, load it through an
import map, and vendor three.js, opentype.js, ffmpeg.wasm and the fonts
with their licences, keeping 3dsvg's licence and credit.

- Keep the editor as it is: the four inputs, every setting, the PNG, video
  (with trimming and MP4 or WebM through ffmpeg.wasm) and 3D model exports,
  the embed code, and the same look. Fix what you find on the way.
- Signed out, keep the design in localStorage. Add sign-in: a round avatar
  at the top right whose menu holds Light, Dark or System, Send feedback
  and Sign out.
- Signed in, Save keeps a shape in member storage with a thumbnail. My
  shapes lists them to open, rename and delete. Mark unsaved changes.
- Any saved shape can get a revocable read-only share link, copied into
  shared storage under a random token and refreshed on each save. Its page
  shows the shape alone with "Edit a copy", and its own link-preview tags.
- Phones first, light and dark, installable with a network-first service
  worker that never caches member data or the video converter.
- For this repository's store, use holm.json version, holm.symbol.svg (one
  black path, no strokes, 0 0 24 24) and listing/listing.json with subtitle,
  category, description, whatsNew and sample screenshots. These are repo
  conventions, not a catalog format promised by the Holm guide.

Run holm app validate --spec-v1 3dsvg. With my approval, deploy with
holm @<peer> app deploy 3dsvg --spec-v1 --host 3dsvg.<my-domain>. Never
replace an occupied host without asking. Validation does not run the app:
test every input and export, a video conversion, two members' saves kept
apart, a share link signed out and after it is turned off, and mobile and
desktop in light and dark. Report gaps honestly. Inspect the target
settings schema before setting sign-in branding.

history.whatsNew: 3dsvg joins the store: the open-source editor rebuilt without a build step, now with sign-in, saved shapes and share links. Videos convert much faster, MP4s are H.264, and exported models face the right way.

apps.name: catalog
apps.title: catalog
apps.description: A store for a repository of Holm apps: a page for every app, and a sheet that installs it on your node.

listing.subtitle: A store for app repositories
listing.description:
The store you're looking at. It lists every app in a repository of Holm apps, gives each one its own page with screenshots, ratings and reviews, and installs it on your node from a Get button. A Get started guide shows newcomers how to set up a node of their own.

Sign in to review an app; reviews appear once an admin approves them. The node's owner and admins get an admin page to show or hide apps, see how often each is viewed and installed, approve reviews and pick the store's colour, and Holm's analytics from the avatar menu.

It reads the repository's index.json, the same file holm app install uses to pick and check a release. Point it at your own repository to give your apps a store of their own.
listing.whatsNew: The avatar menu now has a theme switch: light, dark or the same as your device, remembered in this browser. Tapping the avatar again closes the menu.

All apps as a grid in dark mode: each app's icon with its name under it, in a ruled table, under search and the list or grid switch
The Get started guide: one prompt to copy, beside the store's apps riding a belt into your node
An app's page in dark mode: icon, rating, facts and screenshots
Ratings and reviews on an app's page, with a button to write one
The install sheet: a prompt for your coding agent, written for your node
The admin page: apps with their numbers and a switch to show or hide each one

apps.prompt:
Build a catalog as a Holm App Spec v1 app using only
https://holmhq.com/llms-full.txt for Holm; read sections 9–12 first. Use catalog/
with holm.json, public web/ files, api/main.js exporting
default { async fetch(request, env) }, standard Request/Response, env.holm
storage/auth and env.holm.web.fetch(request) fallback. No build step or
third-party runtime CDN; vendor fonts and any libraries with licenses.

- Define these repository conventions, not a claimed Holm store protocol:
  each top-level app has holm.json version, holm.symbol.svg (one black path,
  no strokes, 0 0 24 24) and listing/listing.json with subtitle, category,
  description, whatsNew and sample screenshots. Write a dependency-free
  Node scripts/index.mjs emitting root index.json: name/path/version,
  <app>/v<version> tag, h1 SHA-256 file fingerprint, size/count, identity,
  symbol path, listing and PROMPT text. Hash sorted app-relative paths and
  file SHA-256 values, then hash those “<hex>  <path>\n” lines and prefix
  the base64 digest with h1:. Exclude listing/ and hidden files; count README
  and PROMPT too. --check detects stale indexes or changed release tags;
  --tag creates missing tags. CI checks then tags versions on main.
- An App Store-like front page: a slideshow of the featured apps' cards
  (no controls; it holds under the mouse, and a mouse drags it),
  then all apps with search (as you type, kept in ?q=) and a list/grid
  switch below it; the grid is ruled like the facts strip (no boxes, lines
  meeting), each near-square cell the icon with its name centred under it,
  no Get and no hover zoom. Each app's own
  /apps/<app> page: icon/colour, version, size, category, license, swipeable
  screenshots, description, whatsNew with a folded version history (the
  index's history: each earlier tag's whatsNew and date), and source
  information. Keep each app's prompt in the index, but don't show it for
  now.
  Read the public repository index with synchronous env.holm.net.fetch,
  not global fetch; cache it in KV and keep the last good index on failure.
- Make it fast: the handler serves every page with the index and the viewer
  embedded, so the first paint waits on no API call (Holm serves a matching
  static file first, so don't name the shell index.html), and preload every
  module. Give each
  /apps/<app> page that app's title, description and listing/cover.png as
  its link preview (a 1200x630 card the repo draws with a script).
- Get opens a sheet remembering my peer/domain, with tabs for
  holm @<peer> app install github.com/<org>/<repo>/<app>@v<version> --host
  <host>, a clone-a-tag holm app deploy <app> --spec-v1, and an agent prompt
  following the app README.
- A /start guide, linked from a header button that stands out and the sheet, for
  someone with no node who will hand the work to a coding agent, never a
  terminal: what Holm is, why a node puts every app here one request away,
  then pick an app and where it runs (this computer, a server, an existing
  node) for a prompt to paste, what the agent asks (the licence is always
  the person's to accept), and the commands folded away. Then building from
  a prompt, what Holm gives an app, links to holmhq.com. Keep it airy.
  Beside its headline, vendor an MIT isometric line-figure kernel and draw
  an interactive figure on it: the apps ride a belt as crates from a store,
  through a gate (the fingerprint check), into a node drum; pointing slows
  the belt and names the crate's app.
- web/llms.txt for that agent: ground rules, the index, and setup, install,
  sign-in and server steps citing sections 4, 5, 8, 9 and 13 of the guide.
  The sheet's agent prompt comes first.
- Sign in through Holm. Signed-in people may rate/review once per app;
  edits wait for approval too. /admin hides apps, moderates reviews, shows
  rough daily views/Get/copy counts in KV and lets me change the tint.
  Authorize each route with documented isAppOwner()/isAppAdmin() checks.
  The guide does not document isNodeOwner()/isNodeAdmin(): do not assume
  those methods or promise node-role access for a fresh build.
- The guide does not document binary net.fetch responses: do not invent
  responseType: 'file'. Keep screenshots as public static files in web/
  until a documented, tested proxy/cache path is available; disclose that
  gap. Make light/dark mobile/desktop layouts, no sideways scrolling, and a
  small Holm/source footer that stays at the bottom over the scrolling page,
  frosted. The avatar menu (a second tap closes it) has a light/dark/
  same-as-device switch, kept in the browser and applied before first
  paint, and Analytics from __HOLM_SURFACES__.

Run holm app validate --spec-v1 catalog. With my approval, deploy with
holm @<peer> app deploy catalog --spec-v1 --host unofficial.<my-domain>.
Check the peer/unused host and explicitly allow the repository's egress host;
ask before replacing a host or moving an older-format app. Inspect target
settings/command help before sign-in branding. Validation is not execution:
test index fetch/failure, screenshots, ownership/admin denials, moderation,
copied deploy commands, mobile/desktop and light/dark. Report all gaps.

apps.name: feedback
apps.title: feedback
apps.description: A button for your website, a QR code for your tables or event. Count the scans, read every word.

listing.subtitle: Feedback for websites, shops and events
listing.description:
Put a feedback button on your website with one script tag, or a QR code on your tables, counter or event badges. People send praise, problems and ideas from their phone, with a photo in one tap and a star rating if you ask for one.

Make it yours: your logo, cover, colour and words on the form, a button that eases in and opens into a panel that springs up, light or dark to match your visitors. A live preview shows every change on a stand-in page, and your site picks it up with the same snippet.

Everything arrives in one inbox per project, ready for hundreds of items: sort it, and filter it by status, time, kind, rating, site or any answer. Keep a thread of notes for your team, see where the button is live, and count how many people scanned, visited and sent something.
listing.whatsNew: Answer by link: file feedback that reached you another way, reply, and send one link that opens it with no sign-in.

screenshots.alt: The feedback form open on a shop's checkout page on a phone, with its cover, a star rating and a message

The Design tab: the project's colour and icon, picked from 48, with the logo beside them
The Form tab: made for a place or event, with a star rating to ask for
Set up: a one-line snippet with its copy button, and the sites where the button is live
Your projects in one panel, each with its icon or logo, its site and what is new
A coffee shop's inbox with 340 items: search, sort, and filters for time, kind, rating, site and its own question
An issue in dark mode, with its screenshot, status and kind
Stats for a project: how many saw a form and how many sent something, per day
Sharing the feedback page: its address, its link and a QR code to print

apps.prompt:
Build a feedback app using https://holmhq.com/llms-full.txt as the only Holm
reference; Holm's own https://github.com/holmhq/cdn is allowed for feed-stars.
Read the v1 sections 9–12 first. Use holm.json with web.spa true, public web/
files and api/main.js exporting default { async fetch(request, env) }.
Use env.holm auth/DS/KV/S3/image, standard Request/Response and same-origin
browser API calls; fall back to env.holm.web.fetch(request). No build step.
Use relative server imports, request.formData() and File.arrayBuffer() for
uploads; no global holm/request/respond and no request.files API.

- Signed-in people make one project per website, shop or event. Supply a
  one-tag widget: a button in a shadow root opens an iframe form; also a
  stand-alone feedback page at a custom address, with SVG QR code/poster.
- Design/Form tabs customize title, words, colour, logo, cover, icon, button
  label/corner/style and theme, with a live preview. Website kinds: Issue,
  Idea, Question; places: Praise, Problem, Idea. Add optional/required stars,
  contact email/phone and up to eight text/select/radio/checkbox questions.
  Support four files, 8 MiB total, and a one-tap phone photo; photo or rating
  alone can send. Shrink big photos in the browser before upload (at most
  2048 px, JPEG quality 0.82), and turn iPhone HEIC photos into JPEG. Strip query/fragment from the sending page's address.
- One private inbox per project: ticket numbers, statuses, notes and a team
  thread, sort/search/filter for hundreds of items. Only the owner sees
  files/contact details. The optional public page shows selected items,
  votes once per browser, and comments only after owner approval. The owner
  can file an item themselves and share one item by an unguessable link
  that needs no sign-in and shows no private fields.
- Keep spam out with a trap field, project caps and allowed sites, honestly
  described as casual-misuse guards, not strong sender authentication.
  Track daily visits, QR/email-link visits, opens, sends, votes and comments
  in app KV; no visitor tracking. “Where it's live” separates local copies.
- Add typed operations for public widget settings and JSON feedback with keyed retries, plus a signed-in owner's private inbox, mark-done, filing and sharing actions and dashboard counts; keep all existing routes and file flows.
- API keys: show once, hash SHA-256, accept bearer tokens on owner routes,
  check project ownership, return the setup snippet; keys cannot mint keys.
- Make it refined on phones/desktop, light/dark/system, a fixed footer and
  scrolling projects panel, avatar menu for keys/theme/stats, /changelog,
  and an optional footer Feedback link to a project I supply.
- Vendor fonts, QR code code and icons with licenses. For feed-stars use
  Holm's CDN pinned to a commit and v-X.Y.Z folder with integrity, plus plain
  stars as fallback. Copy embed.js into other Holm sites when their CSP
  requires it and allow the feedback origin in the site's frame-src.
  The guide does not guarantee frame-ancestors defaults: set deliberate
  web.headers for framing, inspect both responses and test the iframe.
- Make holm.symbol.svg and run holm app identity generate for the icons,
  manifest and social card; author og:image tags only to keep a hand-made
  social preview. Add authored social metadata in web/index.html. Make
  listing/listing.json plus sample screenshots; these are repo conventions,
  not a Holm store schema documented by the guide. Use holm.json version.

Run holm app validate --spec-v1 feedback. With my approval, deploy with
holm @<peer> app deploy feedback --spec-v1 --host feedback.<my-domain>.
Ask before replacing a host or moving an older-format app. Validation does
not run the app: test cross-site embedding, uploads, ownership, comments,
votes/stats and mobile/desktop light/dark. Inspect the target settings schema
before setting sign-in branding. Report any guide or runtime gaps honestly.

apps.name: overlap
apps.title: overlap
apps.description: Find the time that works for everyone. Pick some dates, share one link, and watch everyone's free time overlap, live.

listing.subtitle: Find a time that works for everyone
listing.description:
Pick a few dates and the hours you could meet, then share one link. Everyone paints the times they're free, with just a name and no account, and the grid deepens in colour where people overlap, live, on every open screen.

The best times rise to the top as answers come in, with who can make each one. Pick a time and everyone sees it settle at once, with a calendar file and a Google Calendar link.

Painting plays a soft note for each slot, and the page answers with small motions: it is built to be pleasant to use on a phone and a big screen, in light and dark.
listing.whatsNew: Sign out now ends your session: it posts to Holm instead of following a link.

screenshots.alt: The home page: a headline, a sign-in button, and a small grid filling in as three people answer
A book club plan: five evenings in a grid, deeper green where more of the six people are free
Painting your own free times in coral over a faint view of everyone else's
In dark mode, the settled time in a gold banner with Add to calendar and Google Calendar buttons

listing.subtitle: Private chat for the people on your node
listing.description:
A messenger for the people who share your Holm node. Pick a username, add friends by theirs, and chat one to one or in groups. Messages, typing and unread counts arrive live, on your phone and your desktop at once.

apps.name: sandesh
apps.title: Sandesh
apps.description: Send texts from your own Android phone, in a browser or from your scripts, with India's SMS rules built in.

listing.subtitle: Text from your own phone, from anywhere
listing.description:
Send SMS through the Android phone in your pocket, from any browser or from your own scripts. Install the free SMS Gateway for Android app, paste the username and password it shows, and your texts go out on your own SIM and plan. People see your own number, and their replies come back here.

Each text you send is stamped like a letter as your phone reports it: sent, delivered, or returned when it couldn't get through. Name the people you text, send to up to ten at once, pick a SIM, schedule a text for the morning, and fill in templates you use often. Live receipts arrive the moment your phone has them.

India's SMS rules are built in. A personal SIM is for personal texts, so Sandesh asks before sending anything that reads like an offer or a one-time code, stops at TRAI's limits for bulk texts, and honours every STOP. Templates follow the rules India's DLT system sets for business senders. API keys can be held to a few numbers, so a key that leaks can't text anyone else.

No phone handy? Try the demo phone: it pretends to send, deliver and reply, so you can explore everything first. Light and dark, on a phone or a computer.
listing.whatsNew: Your phone's sign-in is now sealed with standard AES-256-GCM encryption, and the check for same-or-similar texts reads letters in every script, Tamil, Arabic and Thai included. If you connected a phone before this update, connect it once more.

Writing a text that reads like a Diwali sale: Sandesh explains that business texts need a DLT-registered sender and asks you to confirm it's personal before it can be sent
